faqs.question: Should I build a proposal website for someone who is only my crush?
faqs.answer: Usually no. A proposal page is shaped for an answer the sender already knows, and a crush by definition has not given you one. Send something that asks a question they can answer in one word instead.

faqs.question: What should I send if my crush has never given me any signal?
faqs.answer: A plain message in your own words, and no page at all. If you cannot name one specific thing they have done that pointed back at you, an artefact sitting at a URL is more than the situation can carry.

faqs.question: Is it okay to send the page anonymously so they never know it was me?
faqs.answer: No. A page that hides its sender reads as surveillance rather than romance, and it makes the recipient's first task working out who is watching them. It also removes the only thing a yes needs — somebody to say yes to.

faqs.question: Which SubhSandesh template suits asking a crush out?
faqs.answer: The date invitation page, because it asks for a yes or no to one specific outing rather than to a lifetime. The proposal scrapbook is the right template only once you are already together.

faqs.question: How long do people actually spend building one of these pages?
faqs.answer: The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.4 hours, sampled on the /love-gf template across 1,138 pages. That figure is not measured on proposal pages, and it suggests most people keep going back rather than sending in one sitting.

faqs.question: Should I password-protect the page before I send the link?
faqs.answer: Many creators do — 39.9% platform-wide, 1,822 of 4,567 pages across all 16 page types. It limits who else can open the link, but research on privacy-protecting tools indicates protection and disclosure are separate decisions, so the lock does not reduce what you wrote.

faqs.question: Does a page like this work if my crush is in my class or on my team?
faqs.answer: It works badly. Someone who sees you daily in a fixed setting has to manage their answer in front of other people, which turns a private question into a public one.

faqs.question: What happens to the page if they say no?
faqs.answer: Delete it and stop asking. The page can be taken down, but a screenshot cannot, which is the main argument for keeping the first ask small enough to survive a refusal.

faqs.question: Is a marriage-proposal page ever right for a crush?
faqs.answer: Only if the word crush is being used loosely for a partner you are already with. A marriage-proposal scrapbook works because it recounts a shared history, and there is no shared history to recount yet.

faqs.question: Do these pages read properly on a phone?
faqs.answer: Almost half of all views are on a phone — 48.9%, or 25,167 of 51,504 views platform-wide. Assume a small screen, possibly in a room with other people, and write to that.

faqs.question: Can a page say it for me instead of me saying it out loud?
faqs.answer: It can carry the words, but it cannot carry the accountability. If the reason you want a page is to avoid being present for the answer, that is a signal to make the ask smaller rather than more elaborate.

faqs.question: How much should I actually put on the page?
faqs.answer: Less than you will want to once you start. A 551-participant study found the decision of how much to disclose runs on an impulsive system rather than a deliberate one, so fix the size of the ask before you open the builder.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Proposal Website for Crush: What to Send When You Don't Know Yet

A proposal website for a crush is almost always the wrong size of ask, and the fix is a smaller page asking a smaller question. Type *proposal website for crush* into a search box and what comes back is marriage-proposal templates — pages built for an answer the sender already knows.

Two numbers from SubhSandesh's own data set the frame. Platform-wide, across all 16 page types and 4,567 personalised pages built since 12 March 2026, 39.9% of creators password-protect the page before they share it (1,822 of 4,567). Also platform-wide, 92.7% of started pages do get published and shared (4,234 of 4,567), so hesitation is rarely what stops people — over-reach is.

This page covers how to size the page to the signal you actually have, why an unsigned or disguised link reads badly, what the password prompt is really doing, and when to send nothing.

## What a proposal website is, and what it changes

A proposal website is a single link-shareable page built from a template: your photos, your words, an animated sequence, and usually one question with a button at the end. You fill in a form and the page is generated at a URL you send. Nothing is installed and no code is written.

What changes when a question moves out of a chat thread and onto a page of its own is scale. A message can be read and quietly left alone, while a page arrives as an event — it takes a tap and it takes attention.

Platform-wide across all 16 page types, SubhSandesh pages are reopened an average of 11.3 times each. For someone who already loves you, that repeat-opening is the point. For someone who has told you nothing yet, it is a demand wearing the costume of a surprise.

## Match the page to the signal you actually have

The useful question is not "which template" but "how much am I asking them to carry". Four situations follow, in ascending order of what you already know.

Each gives the same four things in the same order: what it is, who it suits, what it asks of the other person, and what it leaves behind if the answer is no.

### 1. No signal at all — send a sentence, not a site

You have talked, you like them, and nothing has ever pointed back at you. This is the case for a plain message in your own words and no page at all.

It suits anyone who could not name one thing the other person has done that suggested interest. It asks them for about ten seconds and one reply. If the answer is no, nothing survives it — there is no artefact sitting at a URL, and that absence is the whole advantage.

### 2. Friendly and warm, nothing said — an invitation with a real plan

They reply quickly, they start conversations, and neither of you has named anything. The right-sized artefact here carries an actual plan — a place, a day, a time — rather than a declaration.

It suits someone who wants the ask to be memorable without being enormous, and it asks for a yes or a no to one afternoon, which is a question a person can answer honestly. A refusal costs a coffee, not a friendship. SubhSandesh's [date invitation page](/date-invitation) is built for exactly this: a yes turns into a countdown, and the plan unlocks one stop at a time on the day.

### 3. Mutual and already flirting — a small page that names it

Something has been said on both sides, or the pattern is obvious enough that neither of you is pretending. Now a page earns its place, because you are confirming something rather than announcing it.

It suits people who have been circling a sentence for weeks, and it asks them to accept a feeling that is already visible — a much lighter lift. The [romantic "I love you" page](/love-gf) is the most-built template on the platform, at 1,138 pages and 24.9% of everything created, which is a fair proxy for how many senders are at this stage rather than the first one.

### 4. Already together — the proposal scrapbook

You are in a relationship and the question is marriage. This is the only one of the four where a full proposal website is proportionate, because the page is a record of a shared history rather than a bid for one.

It suits couples with enough material — photographs, dates, in-jokes — to fill a scrapbook honestly, and it asks for the largest answer a person can give. If that is genuinely where you are, the [proposal scrapbook with a YES button](/proposal) is the template for it, and a crush is not.

## What each route actually costs you

The table compares the four routes on what matters before you build anything. The last column is the one people skip and then regret.

| Route | What it asks for | Build effort | What survives a no |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain message | One reply | Under a minute | Nothing |
| Invitation page with a plan | Yes or no to one outing | Median 6.4 hours of editing, sampled on /love-gf (n=1,138) | A page you can delete |
| Small romantic page | Acceptance of a stated feeling | Median 6.4 hours, same /love-gf sample | A page they may have screenshotted |
| Proposal scrapbook | A life decision | Longest of the four | A permanent, shareable record |

That 6.4-hour median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is sampled on the /love-gf template, not on proposal pages. It says something uncomfortable: people do not build these quickly, they keep going back.

## Why an unsigned or disguised link backfires

There is a strong temptation to send the page without your name on it, or behind a link that looks like something else, so a bad answer never becomes a conversation. Do not.

A page that hides who sent it does not read as mysterious. It reads as surveillance, and the recipient's first job becomes working out who is watching them rather than what the page says.

Research on pseudo-anonymous platforms bears this out rather than softening it. A [mixed-methods study of college students on Yik Yak](https://researchrepository.wvu.edu/faculty_publications/1723) combined twelve in-depth interviews with a content analysis of 3,905 posts from 24 campuses, and describes the resulting phenomena as complex rather than benign. Anonymity changes the message; it is not a neutral wrapper around it.

There is a practical reason too. If they want to say yes, they need to know who to say it to.

## What the password prompt is actually doing

The 39.9% password-protection rate, measured platform-wide across every page type, is not a security feature being used as one. It is a privacy-calculus decision, and there is real research on its shape.

In [an online experiment with 511 participants published in Studies in Communication, Media](https://www.nomos-elibrary.de/10.5771/2192-4007-2021-3-283), Meier, Schäwel and Krämer found perceived privacy risk strongly related to how much protection people wanted, which in turn predicted willingness to use a privacy-protecting tool. Self-disclosure varied by context; protection did not. The lock and the confession are separate decisions, and locking the page does not shrink what you said on it.

An analysis in [Cyberpsychology using three datasets totalling 2,036 respondents](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/15411) found people disclose more when expected gratifications exceed their privacy concerns, and more still when risk and benefit perceptions run high together. A crush page is exactly that combination: the imagined payoff is vivid and the risk is real, so the calculus tips towards saying more.

## The part where you overshoot

Deciding to send something and deciding how much to put in it are not the same decision, and they do not use the same part of your judgement.

A study of 551 adults on a purpose-built social network, [published in Cyberpsychology in 2022](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/15367), separated those two stages. It found that while the reflective, deliberate system may dominate the choice of whether to post at all, an impulsive system appears to take over when deciding how much to disclose. That is the mechanism behind every page that started as a short note and ended as eleven screens.

So decide the size of the ask before you open any builder, write it down, and treat the template as a container with a fixed lid. A [panel survey of 570 social media users in Spain](https://ijoc.org/index.php/ijoc/article/view/22785) found that people who mostly watch rather than post disclose less overall — worth knowing if you have spent months observing this person and are about to reverse that in one evening.

## When a proposal website is the wrong choice

It is the wrong choice whenever you cannot name a specific thing the other person has done that pointed at you. It is also wrong if they are someone you see daily in a fixed setting — a classroom, a team, a shared commute — because a page they cannot answer privately becomes a thing they have to manage in front of other people.

Two mechanical limits matter as well. Platform-wide, 48.9% of views land on a phone (25,167 of 51,504), so a long page is being read on a small screen, in public, possibly next to someone. And a link is a poor substitute when you would rather be able to see their face.

If the answer is no, the answer is no. Delete the page, stop asking, and let the friendship find its own level or not. A second attempt with a bigger page is not persistence; it is pressure, and it is the one outcome this article exists to prevent.

## Sources

- Kezer, M., Dienlin, T., & Baruh, L. (2022). [Getting the privacy calculus right](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/15411). *Cyberpsychology: Journal of Psychosocial Research on Cyberspace*, 16(4).
- Ostendorf, S., Meier, Y., & Brand, M. (2022). [Self-disclosure on social networks: More than a rational decision-making process](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/15367). *Cyberpsychology*, 16(4).
- Meier, Y., Schäwel, J., & Krämer, N. C. (2021). [Between protection and disclosure](https://www.nomos-elibrary.de/10.5771/2192-4007-2021-3-283). *Studies in Communication, Media*, 10(3).
- Clark-Gordon, C. V., Workman, K. E., & Linvill, D. L. (2017). [College Students and Yik Yak](https://researchrepository.wvu.edu/faculty_publications/1723). *Social Media + Society*, 3(2).
- Trifiro, B. M., & Goyanes, M. (2025). [Revealing the True Self Online](https://ijoc.org/index.php/ijoc/article/view/22785). *International Journal of Communication*, 19.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific data exists. A read-only probe of the `proposalpages` collection was refused by this machine's production-read policy in wave 1 and again here, so every SubhSandesh figure in this post is labelled in body prose as platform-wide across all 16 page types, or as sampled on /love-gf. No number is attributed to proposal pages.

The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so this post states no price, no free tier and no paid tier, and sidesteps the cost claim that every competitor on this SERP leads with. Competing pages advertise a price position this post cannot verify or answer.

Phase 1 was inherited, not freshly measured. WebSearch is exhausted at 200/200 for this session, so no live SERP or AI Overview pass was run for 'proposal website for crush'. The competitor picture comes from content/keywords/2026-09-16-propose-100/serps.md and competitor-map.md, measured 2026-09-16 on India-served SERPs, and chiefly from the adjacent keyword 'will you be my girlfriend website proposal'. No position described here should be treated as current.

Four of the five sources were verified from their abstracts rather than their full texts: cyberpsychology.eu served both abstracts in full on the article page; ijoc.org served the abstract on the article page; the Studies in Communication, Media article page at nomos-elibrary.de returned HTTP 200 but serves its abstract through a JavaScript PDF viewer, so the abstract was read from that article's DOAJ record instead; the Yik Yak abstract was read on the West Virginia University repository landing page. All five are open access, none is paywalled, and no claim in the body goes beyond what those abstracts state.
Volume for this keyword is an estimate band with no tool data behind it, so no monthly search volume is printed anywhere in the post.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine would cite this over the five pages on this SERP because it is the only one that answers the question with 'probably do not', names the date-invitation page as the right-sized ask, and attaches real privacy-calculus research plus first-party numbers (39.9% password protection across 4,567 pages, a 6.4-hour median editing gap sampled on /love-gf) that none of bemyval.co, pixeryhub.com, momentocard.in, yourlovepage.online or ai.mobirise.com can publish. The offsetting weakness is that every one of those competitors sells the transaction the searcher came for, while this page talks a share of readers out of it, and the site's domain authority sits below the incumbent operators who hold four of ten slots on the adjacent measured SERP — so movement takes months and is not predicted here.
